package.name: Location
package.author: Peersus contributors
package.description: Explore cities and streets on one interactive globe, with an offline basemap and optional online street detail.

capabilities.location.sharing: Enable location sharing with this paired device. While Location is running, it may obtain and send a fresh position when both devices allow sharing. Turn this off to stop.

exports.description: What the Location page shows, and what a person does on it.

event.description: Answers what a person did on the Location page with the page as it is after it.

exports.description: Carries one position a paired device shared with this one: latitude, longitude, how sure its system was and how old the fix was.

receive.description: Takes the position a paired device shared and keeps it, in memory only, to show on the Location page.

settings.label: OpenStreetMap street detail
settings.help: Show online streets, buildings and place names at close zoom, from OpenFreeMap. OpenFreeMap sees which areas the map shows, also around a device you centre on. Off until you turn it on and approve OpenFreeMap.

settings.label: Keep viewed map areas
settings.help: Keep downloaded map areas on this device (up to 128 MB) to avoid downloads when revisiting. Options shows their count and size and can clear them. When off, only the current view stays in memory; no saved areas are read or written. Previously saved areas stay until cleared.

settings.label: Add Location to page
settings.help: Also show Location as its own page; keep the original Location in these settings.

pages.title: What this extension does
pages.explains: Location has an offline globe and an opt-in mode for online street detail. Enable location sharing separately for each device in Permissions to exchange positions automatically while the extension runs. Browsing the map does not enable sharing. Locate this device displays a local fix; it does not grant sharing permission.
pages.changes: Location is available in extension settings. Adding it to navigation is a separate choice. Locating this device requires permission and the system may also ask. Sharing requires permission for each receiving device. Received positions stay in memory and are forgotten on stop, Forget, unpairing or loss of that device's permission.

body.text: What is sent, and to whom

items: Enable location sharing in Permissions for each device. When a permitted recipient is connected and ready, this extension requests a fix, initially and then at most once every five minutes. Both devices need Location. Turning the sharing permission off stops further sends to that device.
Only to devices you allowed. A paired device receives it only if you allowed Location for it here, and its own person allowed Location for this device there.

Only the position goes to paired devices you allowed: latitude, longitude, how sure your system was and how old the fix is. It travels through the application's encrypted connection, never to the map provider.
How your system finds it is your system's own. Satellites, or the wireless networks it sees, which your system may look up with an online service of its own; Location receives only the position.

The globe works offline by default. Country and city labels and regional roads use public-domain Natural Earth data. The bundled Bucharest and Monaco street data is © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL 1.0).

Online street detail is optional and separately approved. When it is on, OpenFreeMap receives the addresses of the tiles of every area the map shows, including the area around a device you centre on, and can see your network address. Location does not send GPS fixes, shared positions or peer identities to OpenFreeMap. Downloaded tiles are kept on this device, at most 128 MB, unless you turn keeping off; Options says how many are kept and clears them, and removing Location removes them. OpenFreeMap and OpenMapTiles use OpenStreetMap data (ODbL 1.0).
